picks.showTitle: James Low - Dzogchen and Buddhist Teachings
picks.title: Emptiness and dzogchen: the song of the cuckoo. [EN-ES] Granada 10.2014
picks.summary:
Teachings by James Low in Granada, Spain, on "Emptiness and Dzogchen," based on Vairocana's text "The Song of the Cuckoo" (31 October - 02 November 2014).

Original audio in English with consecutive Spanish translation by Juan B. García Lázaro.

"Dzogchen is concerned with knowing your own nature. There are many different paths in Buddhism and gradually they became organised into different styles or families. Some are gradual, others less so, but generally it is a matter of knowing what suits you best." ~ James Low

Full audio recordings available at: https://simplybeing.co.uk/audio-recordings
picks.reason: James Low teaches on emptiness and Dzogchen based on a classic Buddhist text.

What is the one technique that unlocks all benefits instantly while carrying us down the stream unendingly? Can meditation done wrong actually do harm? And why does Zen think death is so funny?? Find out here!

picks.title: Don't Neglect Walking Meditation! | Cankama Bhavana | Dhamma Talk | Jongrom | Ajahn Dhammasiha
picks.summary: Walking meditation is in no way inferior to sitting meditation. In fact, for many of us in modern society it can be a more suitable posture than sitting crosslegged (or even full lotus). The way we grow up, always sitting on chairs, we're often not flexible enough for sitting crosslegged. Therefore, walking can help us to continue our meditation for a much longer time. It's also excellent for excercise, and to keep us fit and healthy. picks.reason: Talk on walking meditation benefits and practice, a core Buddhist meditation method.
